name: Emami Ltd
title: Emami Ltd-$ - 531162 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Consolidated revenue +15% to INR1,039 cr and EBITDA +6% to INR226 cr, but input costs up 360bps and management guides to offset via pricing; no supply-side capacity signal.

summary.headline: Emami Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 15% to INR1,039 crores, but PAT fell 16% to INR137 crores on tax normalisation and input-cost pressure.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 15% to INR1,039 crores and domestic business grew 20% (12% like-to-like, 8% volume after adjusting for Axiom and IncNut). EBITDA rose 6% to INR226 crores and PBT rose 4% to INR195 crores, while PAT fell 16% to INR137 crores due to a higher effective tax rate. Input costs rose 360 bps (about 200 bps from West Asia conflict and 160 bps from business mix), compressing gross margin. International business declined 12% due to West Asia disruption, mainly in OTC pain management, which cannot yet move out of India. Management moved reporting from brand-wise to category-wise.

segments.name: Hair & Scalp care
segments.commentary: Grew 11% in the quarter; Navratna Cool Oil grew strong double digits, Kesh King mid-single digits (management said it is recovering toward double-digit growth by year-end), and 7 Oils in One grew robustly.

segments.name: Skin care
segments.commentary: Grew 3%; Talc portfolio grew high single digits despite regional summer divergence, while Male Grooming and BoroPlus grew low single digits.

segments.name: Healthcare
segments.commentary: Grew 2%; OTC grew high teens (management expects double-digit OTC growth for the rest of the year), Medico grew single digits.

segments.name: Strategic investments (TMC, Brillare, Axiom, IncNut)
segments.commentary: Grew 61% like-to-like and contributes 18% of domestic business; collectively about EBITDA neutral, with gross margins above 50% (TMC above 60%, Brillare and IncNut above 70%). Q1 revenue was about INR160 crores; FY27 guided to INR750-800 crores.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Declined 12% due to West Asia disruption; personal care is produced in UAE, Germany and Thailand and is recovering, but OTC pain management produced in India is still stuck.

guidance_outlook: Management expects to more than offset the absolute increase in input costs during FY27 through further pricing actions.
Management expects the next few quarters to be better than Q1 on margins; it is not worried about margins for the full year.
Talc is expected to return to FY25 levels, with substantially higher numbers in Q2 and for the full year.
International decline expected to be done; significant growth expected in Q3 and Q4 FY27.
Effective tax rate expected at roughly 25-26% for FY27, back to normal taxation of 25%.
Strategic investments: long-term target of high single-digit EBITDA margin at the 3-year point (Dhruv Aggarwal), with Q1 aggregate at about EBITDA breakeven.
Other income to be slightly lower than last year because surplus cash funded the ~INR500 crore Axiom investment and some payments are still pending.
Core business (ex-acquisitions) expected to show better numbers going ahead; management did not give a numeric target.
capex_capacity: Three transformation initiatives (supply chain planning, Sales Code AI, and an enterprise analytics hub) are progressing and expected to complete in FY27.
Acquired businesses (Axiom Ayurveda, IncNut) consolidated from Q1; ~INR500 crore Axiom investment funded internally from surplus cash.
Personal care production sites: UAE, Germany and Thailand; OTC pain management produced in India only.
demand_pricing: Input costs up 360 bps; measured price increases taken in Q1, with further price actions planned.
Quick commerce accounts for 35% of e-commerce business; organized channels 32% of domestic business.
Strategic investments' online split: roughly 20% offline, 25-30% own digital assets and the rest e-commerce, quick commerce and other platforms (overall vertical).
Talc was affected by regional summer divergence; FY26 was a low base for Talc.
Management says growth in low-gross-margin start-ups is the consumer ask and not a concern for overall margins.

qa_highlights.question: Which strategic investment subsegments drove the 61% like-to-like growth and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Dhruv Aggarwal said all four businesses grew substantially in volume and value; TMC grew well above 20%, and growth is expected to remain similar for the rest of the year.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the margin hit is input cost versus structural mix, and will it be offset?
qa_highlights.answer: Mohan Goenka said input costs rose 360 bps, of which about 200 bps was West Asia conflict and 160 bps was mix; pricing is expected to offset the input-cost increase, and he is not worried for the full year.

qa_highlights.question: Will Talc revenue recover to FY25 levels?
qa_highlights.answer: Mohan Goenka said Talc will return to FY25 levels, with substantially higher numbers in this quarter and for the full year.

qa_highlights.question: Can international business recover given Middle East logistics issues?
qa_highlights.answer: Vivek Dhir said personal care supply is recovering, but OTC pain management products are stuck in India pending ministry approvals, expected to resolve in a few days; Goenka expects significant growth in Q3 and Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA margin of the strategic investments and the long-term target?
qa_highlights.answer: Dhruv Aggarwal said the aggregate is about EBITDA neutral, with high single-digit EBITDA expected around the 3-year mark.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Kesh King growth slow and what is the tax-rate outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Goenka said Kesh King grew mid-to-high single digits, expects double-digit growth by year-end, and new D2C launches are planned; Rajesh Sharma said the tax rate should be about 25-26% in FY27.

risks_watch: Gross margin pressure from crude-linked and packaging inflation, with West Asia conflict and commodity costs as key swing factors.
International business: OTC pain management supply from India is still blocked pending approvals; Q3/Q4 recovery depends on this.
Start-ups carry lower gross margins and are EBITDA neutral in aggregate, so mix dilution may persist.
Kesh King growth has slowed to mid-single digits after a revamp, and management acknowledged quarter-to-quarter base effects.
Other income will be lower as surplus cash is used for acquisitions (~INR500 crore Axiom); PAT growth depends on tax normalisation.
Core ex-acquisition growth of about 6% (domestic 6%, per Rajesh Sharma) depends on expected improvement in later quarters.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, the strategic investment portfolio and the second-half recovery, but cautious and somewhat hedged on margins, which management attributed to temporary West Asia pressure. Answers on international OTC supply and the start-up margin path were less specific than the growth commentary.

financial_highlights.change: ~200 bps from West Asia conflict, ~160 bps from mix

key_quotes: So, we would be able to recover and go back to the '25 numbers.
Dhruv Aggarwal: I think you will see something similar. So this is quite sustainable.
And out of which almost 200 basis points is due to the conflict, West Asia conflict and the balance 160 is because of the mix.
I'm not worried for the whole year, Arnab, very honestly.
And on the international front, I think the decline, this is now done.
It should be around 25%, 26% Vaibhav this year because still last year, we were enjoying some fiscal benefits.
Kesh King is back on traction.
But I think you would expect high single digit probably at the 3-year point, and then we'll take it from there.

growth.why: Management guides to strong start-up revenue of INR750-800 crores in FY27, double-digit OTC and Kesh King growth by year-end, and international growth in Q3-Q4, backed mainly by announced price increases and a recovering Talc portfolio rather than capacity or order book; no revenue growth % or capacity additions were quantified.
